What is the solution around a profit driven game development structure?

Expect less money out of more niche games. It's that simple. Companies making games these days seem to somehow not understand this basic concept. They also don't seem to understand how to organize a company, or treat their employees well, or how to exist as an entity that makes money to survive rather than survive just to chase profits. I think it's less a problem with the system, more a problem with the businesses themselves. It's possible to make better, more niche games that garner overall less money and still be profit driven.

Pretty simple really.

Show us you are able to deliver on a game by providing enough of showcases. Good game devs get funded easy like that. If you don't have anything at all to show for, well it's a matter of:

"why should i fund you if all you have is ideas?"

possibly profit sharing with the players, create games that have league play in mind, in game purchases are so common now that who would really blink an eye if a team of 12 had to pitch in 5 a head to play another team in a face off, that is 120 on the table right there, the game takes 20, leaving 100 to the team that wins said match, divided by 12 is 8 bucks and some change. now modify that and make a bracket playoff and the numbers grow rather large pretty fast. keep all the money in player accounts and when they want to cash out use a service to fund the request, just not paypal, f#$k paypal. the introduction of gaming for money is already done, just bring that experience to the player at home as opposed to professional gamers. The solution, really, is for us to be a little bit more careful in thinking games are different from any other product we might buy. We don't question why car companies operate for profit, or restaurants, or skilled trades building, renovating, and repairing homes. People drag themselves out of the house every day with the hopes of earning a living to support themselves and, in many cases their family, with a dream somewhere that they'll earn enough to live a little better, perhaps retire a little sooner. Nothing wrong with any of that.
